We exchanged greetings, and Chief Bogoljub Janicevic briefly spoke to me, saying that the PJP under the command of the staff for combatting terrorism from Pristina was carrying out an operation of breaking up terrorist strongholds, but that we as the police station have nothing to do with that and that we should continue our regular activities. I spent a bit more time there with my assistants who had stayed on at the police station, namely Zoran Djordjevic and Aleksandar Simic. I gave them some brief instructions along the following lines: They should keep the shift that had been prepared until this event crystallises, or rather, to see whether any logistical support would be needed for that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Please, you said if logistical support would be needed for that action. What kind of logistical support or assistance in relation to the police station in Stimlje, if I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing special. We had two medical vehicles that were on duty there if the wounded were supposed to be transported to hospital. That would be it because they had their own line of supplies. Under their command they carried all of that out separately, so nothing special happened there except that the shift should stay there prepared if anything is needed, say, an on-site investigation or other regular police work that we were supposed to carry out. I left Stimlje at around 9.00 or 9.30 a.m., I can't remember exactly, I left the police station at Stimlje. Nothing unusual happened on that day. Shooting could be heard from the area of Racak in the hills above Racak and Petrovo. We went on. We carried out the change of shifts, and I stayed in Crnoljevo until the 20th, and it's only on the 21st that I returned to Stimlje due to certain necessities of my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mladenovic. Now I'd like to go back to some of the things you mentioned for the sake of clarification, things that matter to me, actually. Tell me, when you came to the police station in Stimlje, did you notice any units, any PJPs that were not from the police station of Stimlje or any other members of PJPs?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: I did not notice anything special at the police station. Things were running as usual except Radomir Mitic was present there and Bogoljub Janicevic, chief of SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And tell me, when you entered your office and when you found the chief of SUP there and the head of the police squad, was anyone else there with them in that office?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: No. In front of that office there were only two of my assistants, Simic and Djordjevic. And in the office, in my office, it was only Chief Bogoljub and Mitic, no one else.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, did you see then in any office or anywhere in or around the police station in Stimlje, did you see Mr. Vladimir Djordjevic there anywhere?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see him anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you repeat to me once again around what time you arrived at the police station and when you left it, how much time did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact time, but I think that we left Urosevac around 8.30. Now, how much time we needed to get to Stimlje, let's say it was up to half an hour. And then in Stimlje we spent not more than half an hour. So it is possible that I was there up to 9.30 at the latest or say up until 10.00 -- in the morning, that is, that's what I'm talking about. That would be it roughly. I cannot remember the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, you said that Djordjevic, if I'm not mistaken, your assistant was at the office on that day. Did he ever inform you that he saw General Djordjevic on the 15th of January on the premises of the Stimlje police station?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: On the 15th of January no one informed me that General Djordjevic had been there or that he had come at all. It was only the chief of SUP and the chief of the police squad who were in my office. That's what my assistants told me. It's only when I came to the police station in Stimlje on the 20th, due to certain commitments of my own that I had there, my assistants informed me that General Djordjevic had come on the 18th, only three days after this particular event. Over those three days, the 15th, the 16th, the 17th, and the 18th, they had engaged in heavy fighting, the PJPs, especially with the terrorist strongholds. And that due to these problems, an on-site investigation could not have been carried out. They tried to carry out an on-site investigation on the 15th and on the 16th, and it was only on the 18th that they managed to carry out an on-site investigation. When General Djordjevic came and he personally sent out Radomir Mitic, the chief of the police squad, to carry out that duty. The assumption was that one of the assistants would be sent on that mission with a security detail because they belonged to the police station in Stimlje; however, General Djordjevic then ordered that the chief of the station go with the on-site investigation team. So the assistants remained and that is the direct knowledge I had about that. Also, they informed me that in the fighting and in the attacks from a Browning, from the so-called northern hill, which is a place between Petrovo and Malo Poljce, in the area of the village of Luzac there was a terrorist base there. They used a Browning to fire at the police station. The police station was hit, and I think that that is documented, that an on-site investigation was carried out and also that photo documentation was compiled with how many projectiles the police station in Stimlje had been hit. I was informed about that and that was it for this particular period of time. I don't know what else you're interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Before the 20th, as you said, did you know who carried out the Stimlje operation or in any -- or in which way this was done?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: As I said a few moments ago, I received some brief information from the chief of SUP on that day when I arrived at the police station, when I stopped briefly there on the 15th that what was being carried out was a police action by members of the PJPs. I don't know which ones and I don't know what their numbers were. It was only that this action was being carried out by the members of the PJPs under the command of the staff for combatting terrorism in Pristina. The staff was under the command of General Sreten Lukic. That is the same thing that I learned from my assistants when I came back to the police station on the 20th.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, I'm referring to the 20th now. When you arrived then, did you receive any information to the effect that this action had been portrayed as a massacre of civilians and the verifiers were already making statements in this regard?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: Statements were well underway that this had been a massacre that civilians had been executed and things like that. That's the kind of information that was bandied about. There was even a radio from the area held by the KLA operating somewhere from Drenica, between 15- and 1700 hours. On that radio they were providing information allegedly that the Serb police had carried out a massacre of civilians; that was never proven of course. Because these were fighters from the so-called KLA, UCK they called themselves. That means in translation the Kosovo Liberation Army. That is that terrorist Albanian organisation that engaged in combat in that area in that period of time. Later, of course, when an on-site investigation was carried out Finnish pathologists and our pathologists corroborated that. These were not civilians, rather, they were members of the KLA for Racak, the commander was Sadik Mujota. We all knew that. He was a man who openly conveyed a message to all, that he had joined the Kosovo Liberation Army, as they called themselves, and that they -- and that he would not stop before he enters the police station and has a cup of coffee there. Those were his words. His camp was near the police station at Racak at a point called Cesta. From there his intention was to place under his control together with his terrorist unit all of Stimlje. Of course he did not succeed in doing that because that group had been crushed on time. He got killed then, if I remember correctly, together with his sons, Fatmir -- Fadil, I can't remember hat their names were exactly, and his daughter got killed there too. He also had two brothers who were involved in all of this. Before that we had had some intelligence, we had the names of all of those who were casualties there, and they all belonged to this organisation, and for the most part they came from those villages, Racak, Petrovo, Malo Poljce, and there were people who came from elsewhere like Vitina and, I don't know, other towns and villages in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me now, after these events and the information you received, when did you return from the duty shift from Crnoljevo?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: I returned from Crnoljevo after 15 days, probably on the 30th of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thanks. Do you know anything about the burial that -- the burial of the people who had lost their lives in that operation in Racak, the burial that should have taken place?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After a while I was back at the Stimlje police station and there were problems again. They -- the problems were with the bodies claimed by the families. I think it was on the 10th of February, 1999, after the autopsy of the bodies. The bodies were transported and -- they were transported to Stimlje and Danica Marinkovic, an investigative magistrate, escorted that transport. This was arranged with the OSCE verifiers and the Albanian families. I was in -- directly informed of that by Bogoljub Janicevic, the chief of the SUP. I'm not sure what time it was exactly, but it was winter-time. After 4.00 p.m. -- before that at the police station they were already the local Muslim priest of Stimlje. In the centre of the town there was a mosque where he held religious services, and he was the -- there was also the president of the Democratic League of Kosovo. He was the president of that organisation in Stimlje. They came to see me in my office together with the verifiers. They were eight in all or nine, I believe. Before they had -- before they brought the bodies, TV teams had arrived and other verifiers. The verifiers then started asking awkward questions about whether we would intervene if members of the KLA would arrive with the families. These people were in Racak and Petrovo, and I answered in the affirmative because to us, the police, they were members of a terrorist organisation, and we will try to arrest them. However, he said that we must withdraw all patrols and that all police had to go away so that the families can take over the bodies, and that's when the problem arose. I don't know the man in person, but it was Colonel Mijatovic from the staff in Pristina who had told them they could bury the bodies at Cesta, which is in Racak. That's where they were killed actually. As there was no cemetery, no religious burial grounds, I said that wasn't possible because dead bodies are buried on religious burial grounds. You cannot simply bury people where they come to death. And that certain permits are required for cemeteries, permits issued by municipal authorities. And when the problem arose he said to the investigative magistrate, one of the verifiers I mean, "How do you want to hand over the bodies if the families aren't here to claim them?" And then he directly accused Danica Marinkovic of playing games with the bodies. She had brought the bodies to Stimlje and nobody was killing to claim them and that's where the problem arose. After that Danica Marinkovic, the investigative magistrate, decided to return the bodies to Pristina, and she informed the families that they could come to the hospital chapel in Pristina and claim the bodies there. That's what I know about the event which happened on the 10th in Stimlje. On the following days, if you want me to continue --

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, did the burial take place?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the burial took place. In the morning the Albanian families organised themselves. I'm not sure how. Anyway, we were informed that they would claim the bodies on their own and they would bury them in the mosque at Racak. On the same day around 10.00 or 11.00 the bodies were transported on the road through Stimlje because that road led to the centre of Racak. The bodies were taken to the mosque first and there was media coverage and it was also covered by the verifiers. The locals of those villages may have received orders to that effect or maybe it was their genuine wish to attend the burial. But anyway, a large number gathered in Racak for the burial. From what we were able to see, the dead were buried like soldiers with Albanian flags wrapped around their coffins, which is not the custom when you bury a dead Albanian. After the burial we were able to observe that at the burial there were persons in uniform, armed persons who were members of the so-called Kosovo Liberation Army, the terrorist organisation. They attended the burial in significant numbers and subsequently they kidnapped about 50 Albanians from the crowd. Among them two brothers of our reserve police officers from the Olluri family, from the Petrovici village, and some other Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mladenovic. I'll ask you some more questions about this and show you some documents, but I will need a rather lot of time to do that. So as it's roughly time for the break with the leave of the Trial Chamber we might as well break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we'll have the second break now and resume in half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down. Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we next please have D150.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It's your tab 17. Mr. Mladenovic, this is a report on Albanians kidnapped by terrorists from a funeral in Racak village dated 12th February, 1999. Please acquaint yourself with the report shortly and tell us, please, whether the information contained therein tallies with the information you had about the event.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This was quite indicative of that period. On the 12th of February several Albanians were kidnapped who attended the funeral. Rexhep and Muhamed Olluri were members of the reserve police force in Stimlje. They were kidnapped on that occasion. They were loyal citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 we see another name.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Zeqiri Basri who reported to the Stimlje police station that on the 11th of February during the funeral in Racak, Stimlje municipality, terrorists kidnapped his cousin Zeqir Hyseni about 50 years old from Stimlje, former employee of the Pristina district prison. He came to Racak village with his wife Hysnia in a blue Zastava 101 passenger vehicle. We insisted that the OSCE KVM take all measures to liberty these people. Concerning these kidnappings, on that same day we notified the verification mission representatives who were in Stimlje. They promised to do everything in their ability to try and liberate these citizens.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. We'll see another document which confirms that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D010-0785, D010-0785. That's the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 18. It's a report dated 12 February 1999. You can read to yourself what the contents are about and please tell us whether it's what you have just referred to.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was drafted the next day in the police station by the police station commander in Stimlje, warrant officer Zoran Djordjevic. He was in touch with certain OSCE mission representatives who were in Stimlje. They came to the police station, telling him that they saw the commander promising to come back with certain information in the afternoon. In the meantime they went to the village of Petrovo, where they had a discussion with the terrorists, who promised them that people will be released in two hours' time. These people had been kidnapped the previous day. The person in question were Mehmet and Rexhep Olluri and Hysen Zeqiri. They promised them to release these people within the next two hours. They had learned that morning of those people being kidnapped in the Stimlje police station. The persons in question were Mehmet and Rexhep Olluri and Hysen Zeqiri. They wanted to know whether we had any information on any other persons who had been kidnapped. That's it. This follows the previous documents. The verifiers had been informed and the next day they came to the police station. I wasn't there at the moment. The assistant commander was there. It says here that they were there between 6.10 and 6.15 p.m. They were only there for a brief period of time. The persons had been kidnapped on the 11th and were held until the 12th and around 8.00 p.m. on that day they were released.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: We'll see some other documents testifying to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll seek to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00820.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D010-0788.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 19. We see that this report is dated 13 February 1999. Please read to yourself what the report is about and tell us briefly whether this corresponds to the information you had.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO MLADENOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. This is another report drafted in the Stimlje police station. This was the following day after the document -- the day we saw the previous document about. It was the 13th of February. The report was drafted by a police station deputy commander, Mr. Mitrovic. This report was also drafted at 6.10 p.m. following his meeting with the verifiers who told him that in their negotiations with the terrorists they managed to secure the release of the persons mentioned here, Taib Zeqiri, Jemer Xherimi and Jakup Ibali. There were several people who had been kidnapped. They did try to have all of them released. We saw the previous document referring to those three people and here we have additional three people subsequently released by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I move to have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D00821.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'd like to move to a completely different topic, which has to do with certain allegations I wanted to put to the witness concerning the testimony of K-86 before this Tribunal. For that purpose I wanted to quote certain parts of the transcript and ask this witness to comment. Most of that transcript was in closed session, hence I propose we do the same now so as to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will now adjourn. We resume tomorrow at 2.15. We must adjourn overnight now. An officer will assist you during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 9th day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
